extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents and third-party submitters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing statutory invention registrations (SIR), 18-month publication of U.S. patent applications (pre-grant publication/PGPub), the content/timing of patent application publications, requests to avoid or correct publication, and third‑party preissuance submissions under 37 CFR 1.290.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR timeliness (requests before March 16, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only requests for a statutory invention registration filed prior to March 16, 2013 are timely; requests filed on or after March 16, 2013 will not be treated because pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 157 was repealed on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on requests filed before March 16, 2013 may be found in the earlier MPEP materials (former MPEP §§ 1103-1109).

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR publication obligations and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for a statutory invention registration is approved the statutory invention registration will be published and a notice of the publication will be published in the Official Gazette; the SIR will be mailed to the requester at the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published SIRs are sequentially numbered in a separate 'H' series (starting with H1); see MPEP § 901.04(a) for kind codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR published statement about attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each published SIR will include the statement: 'A statutory invention registration is not a patent. It has the defensive attributes of a patent but does not have the enforceable attributes of a patent. No article or advertisement ... may use the term patent ... when referring to a statutory invention registration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more specific information on rights associated with an SIR see 35 U.S.C. 157.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR treated as prior art and constructive reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 157(c), a published SIR will be treated the same as a U.S. patent for all defensive purposes and usable as a reference as of its filing date; a SIR is a 'constructive reduction to practice' under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) and 'prior art' under applicable sections of 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIRs are classified, cross-referenced, placed in search files, disseminated to foreign offices, stored in USPTO databases, and announced in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR waiver effects on patentability of related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The waiver of patent rights to subject matter claimed in a SIR takes effect on publication and may affect patentability of claims in related applications (e.g., divisionals or continuations) to the extent the same invention is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply standards similar to 'same invention' double patenting determinations to decide whether a waiver in a SIR precludes patenting by the same inventor in related applications; rejections based on SIR waiver cannot be overcome by a terminal disclaimer; holder of a SIR cannot recapture waived rights by reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule: eighteen-month publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, each nonprovisional utility and plant application filed on or after November 29, 2000 will be published promptly after the expiration of a period of 18 months from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought (pre‑grant publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application may be published earlier at applicant's request; publication is governed by 35 U.S.C. 122(b) and 37 CFR 1.211.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will not be published if it is (i) no longer pending, (ii) national security classified/subject to secrecy order, (iii) has issued as a patent in time to be removed from publication process, (iv) filed with a compliant nonpublication request, and further exceptions include provisional applications, design applications, international design applications, and reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion to a provisional or other after‑file action does not automatically remove an application from publication unless recognized in sufficient time; technical preparations for publication generally begin four months prior to projected publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication basis and earliest filing date calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are normally published based on the application as filed; publication occurs after eighteen months from the earliest of (1) the U.S. filing date, (2) the international filing date, or (3) the filing date of an earlier application for which a benefit is claimed (35 U.S.C. 119,120,121,365,386).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to timely submit priority/benefit claims to ensure proper publication timing and avoid petitions under 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 and surcharges under 1.17(t).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness requirement prior to publication (basic items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not publish an application until it includes the basic filing fee and any required English translation; in accordance with 37 CFR 1.211(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these items are missing, publication will be delayed until corrected; see MPEP § 1121 for additional required content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other content that may delay publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may delay publication until the application includes required application size fees, a specification in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52, an abstract in compliance with 37 CFR 1.72(b), drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84, sequence listing or sequence listing XML (if applicable), and an oath/declaration or application data sheet with required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submission quality is insufficient to create the publication, the Office will issue a preexamination notice requiring substitute specification or replacement drawings and will use the applicant's reply for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office refusal/exclusion for legal or offensive material
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may refuse to publish an application, or include portions thereof, if publication would violate Federal or state law, or if the application or portion contains offensive or disparaging material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require a substitute specification to delete offending material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee and payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d) must be paid in each application published under this section before the patent will be granted; the notice of allowance will include the publication fee which must be paid within three months from mailing of the notice of allowance to avoid abandonment (no extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is not published, any paid publication fee will be refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected publication date and technical preparation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the application is complete, the Office will provide a projected publication date on the filing receipt; the projected date normally will be the later of 18 months from earliest filing date or 14 weeks from mailing of the filing receipt; technical preparations for publication generally begin four months before the projected date and publication occurs on Thursdays; publication process takes about 14 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should promptly review filing receipts and request corrections to assist Office processing before technical preparation/export to the publisher begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding publication via express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid publication by express abandonment, an applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c); unless the applicant has received a notice of abandonment at least 4 weeks prior to projected publication, a petition is required to expressly abandon and avoid publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting an application to become abandoned by failing to reply (passive abandonment) risks the Office not recognizing abandonment in time to avoid publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to provisional insufficient to avoid publication unless timely recognized
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting a nonprovisional application to a provisional will not avoid publication of the nonprovisional unless the request to convert is recognized in sufficient time to remove the application from the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot ensure removal from publication any time after technical preparations have been initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication content: front page, drawings, specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application publication includes a front page containing information similar to a patent front page, the drawings (if any), and the specification (including claims); generally based on the application papers and drawings deposited on the filing date and the executed oath/declaration or ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication may also include certain subsequent amendments if submitted in time to be entered into the file wrapper before technical preparation begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of assignee information
rubrics_metrics.description: If provided in the application data sheet (ADS) filed with the application (37 CFR 1.46), the patent application publication will include the name of the assignee or person to whom the inventor is obligated to assign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignee info on the ADS does not substitute for recording an assignment per part 3 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to base publication on an amended EFS copy (timing & compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: At applicant's option, the publication may be based on a copy of the application (specification, drawings, ADS/oath) as amended if the applicant supplies such a copy compliant with USPTO EFS requirements within one month of mailing date of the first Office communication that includes a confirmation number, or within fourteen months of the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the EFS copy does not comply with requirements, the Office will publish based on the originally filed papers; if the publication process has not started, an untimely but usable copy may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments inclusion window and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that are entered into the application file before technical preparations (generally 4 months prior to projected publication) may be used in the publication (substitute specification, amended abstract, complete claim listing, amended drawings), but the Office cannot guarantee inclusion of any particular or latest amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For drawings or other changes to be included, replacement materials must be entered into the file wrapper in sufficient time (before four months prior to projected publication date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid filing preliminary amendments with the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not file preliminary amendments with the application because submitting an application without preliminary amendments reduces Office processing and helps ensure publications are printed correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure under 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1). Substitute specifications are generally required for preliminary amendments to the specification (other than claims); applicants should not file substitute specifications with the application because the application size fee will be calculated on both clean and marked versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for republication to correct publication errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of errors in the patent application publication and inclusion of desired amendments into the originally filed specification/drawings requires filing a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.221(a); errors will not be corrected by a corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1130 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of appendices and large sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices (other than sequence listings, sequence listing XMLs, or large tables) are not printed if they are on pages after the claims; lengthy sequence listings or sequence listing XMLs (>= ~600 Kb) are not printed with page image versions and will be published only in electronic form with a hyperlink in the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer program listings may be printed if included in the specification before the claims; computer program listing appendices submitted on optical disc or via EFS are not printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant information errors not treated as material mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in applicant information printed on the publication (e.g., assignee name) are not considered material mistakes by the Office under 37 CFR 1.211(b) and thus may only be corrected by filing a request for republication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1130 for processing republication requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission compliance screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions under 37 CFR 1.290 will not be automatically entered into the application file; they will be reviewed by the Office to determine compliance with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290 before being entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliant submissions will be entered and made available to examiners; paper submissions incur more processing delay than electronic submissions via the dedicated web interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire-submission-entry rule (partial non-compliance prevents entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any part of a third-party submission that is not in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290 will prevent entry of the entire third-party submission into the record; however, if the submission is compliant with 122(e) but non‑compliant with some requirement of 37 CFR 1.290, minor errors that do not raise ambiguity may, at the Office's discretion, be tolerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not attempt to enter portions of partially compliant submissions; determinations are case‑by‑case and at the sole discretion of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant third-party submissions discarded; fees not refunded
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-compliant third-party submissions (except those with minor non‑compliance tolerated) will not be entered into the file wrapper or considered and will be discarded; required fees will not be refunded in such cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory time period for making a third-party submission will not be tolled by an initial non-compliant submission; a third party may file another complete submission if the statutory period has not closed (a fee may be required for resubmission after non-compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission filing methods and format restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions may be filed electronically via the dedicated web-based interface (preferred) or in paper by first-class mail, USPS Priority Mail Express®, or hand delivery; submissions may not be filed by facsimile and paper filings will be delayed by scanning/indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing provides immediate electronic acknowledgment; paper filers may include a self-addressed postcard to receive an acknowledgment by return receipt postcard (which only confirms receipt, not compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission content requirements (concise description etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions must include the items and concise descriptions required by 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290 (e.g., identification of documents and concise descriptions of relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a concise description of relevance is missing or improper, the submission will be non-compliant and not entered; the notification of non-compliance will include reasons (if an email address was provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party involvement limitations and ex parte prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The involvement of a third party ends with filing the submission; a third party will not receive communications from the Office regarding the submission except electronic acknowledgement, return postcard, or a notification regarding the third-party submission; a third party is not permitted to contact the examiner or respond to the examiner's treatment of the submission because patent prosecution is ex parte.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about submissions may be directed to the point of contact listed on Office notifications regarding the third-party submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner treatment of compliant third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once screened and found compliant, a third-party submission will be entered into the file wrapper for examiner consideration; the examiner should consider the listed publications and concise descriptions in the same manner as information in an IDS, generally before issuing the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should sign form PTO/SB/429 (or equivalent) to indicate items were considered, clear the submission's IDS flag in the Patent Data Portal, and provide a signed copy of PTO/SB/429 with the next Office action. The examiner's signature does not indicate agreement with the third party's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant response not required to third-party submission absent Office request
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.290(h), in the absence of a request by the Office, an applicant need not reply to a third-party submission; if the Office believes information from the applicant is needed, it may issue a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no circumstance where an examiner may direct a requirement for information to the third party who submitted the paper under 37 CFR 1.290.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing and distinguishing third-party cited documents on issued patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents from third-party submissions that were considered by the examiner will be printed on the patent and will be distinguished from documents cited by the applicant and by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner determines a listed document should not be considered (e.g., is not a publication), the examiner should consult the screener/TC contact and may strike through the document to indicate it was not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications regarding third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may request a courtesy email notification of compliance/non‑compliance when filing electronically or by including a paper request with a paper submission; notifications of non-compliance will state reasons if an email address was provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notification will be issued if the third party does not provide an email address or where the submission is directed to an unpublished application; notification is not made of record in the application and the Office does not plan to record the email address in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant notification of compliant submissions (e-Office Action participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant will be notified upon entry of a compliant third-party submission in their application file where the applicant participates in the Office's e-Office Action program, and the contents will be made available to the applicant after entry; applicants will not be notified of non-compliant submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may view non‑patent documents identified in a third-party document list via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed forms for petitions and submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain petitions and requests relating to publication and pre-grant procedures should use specified forms (examples given: Form PTO/AIA/24A or PTO/SB/24A for Petition for Express Abandonment to Avoid Publication; PTO/SB/35 for Nonpublication Request; PTO/SB/36 for Rescission of Nonpublication Request and Notice of Foreign Filing; PTO/SB/64a for Revival petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are available on the USPTO website under Patent Forms; consult MPEP §§ 1122-1125 and § 1135 for use guidance.
